You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Night-boat loaders call `/opt/ferry/bin/cleat` with `stow --roll` and `--chalk`. Chalk is overwritten. `/app/dock/harbour.md` is the house book for roll grammar, chalk fields, and reject codes. `/app/dock/lane-cards.md` holds per-lane centimetre span, height lids, kilogram lids, and paired deck kilograms. `/app/dock/discharge.md` is the book for boarding seats, last-on-first-off stations, neighbour gaps, and the ramp keep-clear. Sample rolls live in `/app/rolls`. The incomplete source package directory `/app/environment` must be updated until the installed binary matches those books. `/app/bollard/preview.go` is a leftover sketch, not the graded binary.

Short freight that clears the lower lid still takes a tall-lid berth. Two heavies that still fit the shorter leftover centimetres both remain on that leftover. A third medium that still fits leftover kilograms still shares that deck. Two unbalanced heavies plus a 5500 kg follow-on still share one deck. A later-boarded plate sits deeper than an earlier one. A long plate printed first still keeps the shorter leftover while an earlier boarded short plate is pushed off that leftover. Two flagged plates still sit only one keep-clear apart. A long vessel whose length still fits the painted span still occupies the shorter leftover.

The verifier reruns `/opt/ferry/bin/cleat` on held-out rolls and reads the chalk NDJSON with `i`, `verb`, `plate`, `deck`, `lane`, `station`, and `ok`.

--- harbour ---
# Harbour stow book

Call `/opt/ferry/bin/cleat stow --roll PATH --chalk PATH`.
Rolls are UTF-8, one command per line. Blank lines and `#` comments are
skipped. Fields are spaces or tabs. Plate names are letters, digits, period,
underscore, or hyphen. Length, height, mass, hazmat, and board numbers are
unsigned decimals. Anything else is malformed (exit 2).

```
PLATE name LEN cm HT cm MASS kg HAZ 0|1 BOARD n
```

`LEN`, `HT`, and `MASS` must be greater than zero. `HAZ` is `0` or `1`. `BOARD`
is a positive boarding sequence: smaller numbers drive on first. Equal `BOARD`
values load in ascending plate name.

An empty roll writes an empty chalk file and exits 0. Chalk is replaced with
NDJSON. `i` starts at 1; every input plate yields one `stow` row in listing
order, not packing order. Successful `ok` is `yes`; otherwise `no`. `verb` is
`stow`. A plate that cannot fit is not placed: `ok` is `no` and `deck`, `lane`,
and `station` are omitted.

Lane lids live on `/app/dock/lane-cards.md`. Seats, stations, and keep-clear
distances live on `/app/dock/discharge.md`.
--- lane cards ---
# Lane cards

Search order is `A1`, `A2`, `B1`, `B2`.

| Lane | Height lid (cm) | Span (cm) | Mass lid (kg) |
| A1 | 180 | 2000 | 8000 |
| A2 | 180 | 2000 | 8000 |
| B1 | 420 | 2000 | 18000 |
| B2 | 420 | 2000 | 18000 |

Deck `A` also has a paired kilogram lid of 11000 that both `A1` and `A2` share.
Deck `B` has a paired kilogram lid of 28000 that both `B1` and `B2` share.
Sister lanes on a deck must stay within 3000 kg of each other once both sisters
already hold a plate. Opening the first plate on a deck is free. Opening the
second sister lane is free.

Kilograms already packed in a lane count against that lane's mass lid. Kilograms
already packed on the same deck letter count against the paired lid. A plate
that fits leftover centimetres but not leftover lane kilograms, or that would
break the paired lid or sister trim, must try the next lane. Leftover is
computed after earlier boarding seats, not after the order the names appear in
the roll.

Decks: `A` lid 180 cm; `B` lid 420 cm. Low plates that still fit on `A` must
not occupy `B`.
--- discharge ---
# Discharge seats

Search order is on the lane cards. Seat plates in increasing `BOARD`, then
plate name. Remaining length, lane kilograms, paired deck kilograms, and sister
trim are those of plates already seated.

Remaining length includes the neighbour keep-clear and, for a hazmat plate, a
100 cm ramp keep-clear beyond its own length. The ramp keep-clear is empty of
other plates and does not move that plate's ramp-facing station. A clean plate
does not take a ramp keep-clear.

If a previous plate already sits in that lane and either plate has `HAZ=1`,
leave 100 cm empty before the new length. If both plates have `HAZ=1`, leave a
second 100 cm. The first plate in a lane never takes a leading gap.

A plate's `station` is centimetres from the ramp to its ramp-facing face. On a
2000 cm lane a 400 cm earliest plate sits at station 1600. The earliest packed
plate in a lane sits deepest. Later plates sit nearer the ramp. Chalk rows stay
in listing order.

package main

import (
        "fmt"
        "os"
)

func main() {
        if len(os.Args) != 6 || os.Args[1] != "stow" || os.Args[2] != "--roll" || os.Args[4] != "--chalk" {
                fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "usage: cleat stow --roll PATH --chalk PATH\n")
                os.Exit(2)
        }
        body, err := os.ReadFile(os.Args[3])
        if err != nil {
                os.Exit(1)
        }
        rc, text := fold(string(body))
        if err := os.WriteFile(os.Args[5], []byte(text), 0644); err != nil {
                os.Exit(1)
        }
        if rc == -2 {
                os.Exit(2)
        }
        if rc != 0 {
                os.Exit(1)
        }
}

package main

import "strings"

func fold(sheet string) (int, string) {
        cars, rc := parseRoll(sheet)
        if rc != 0 {
                return rc, ""
        }
        if len(cars) == 0 {
                return 0, "{\"i\":1,\"verb\":\"stow\",\"ok\":\"empty\"}\n"
        }
        ordered := arrange(cars)
        fill := map[string]*occ{}
        deckKg := map[string]int{}
        var lines []string
        n := 0
        for i, car := range ordered {
                lane := pickLane(car, fill, deckKg)
                station := stationOf(2000, car, 0)
                _ = i
                emit(&lines, &n, car.Plate, lane.Deck, lane.Name, fmtInt(station), "yes")
                if fill[lane.Name] == nil {
                        fill[lane.Name] = &occ{}
                }
                fill[lane.Name].used += car.Len
                fill[lane.Name].has = true
        }
        return 0, strings.Join(lines, "")
}

func fmtInt(n int) string {
        if n == 0 {
                return "0"
        }
        sign := ""
        if n < 0 {
                sign = "-"
                n = -n
        }
        var d []byte
        for n > 0 {
                d = append([]byte{byte('0' + n%10)}, d...)
                n /= 10
        }
        return sign + string(d)
}

Analysis: The parser currently expects the wrong token layout and silently skips malformed lines, explaining why the valid sample was treated as empty. The implementation also lacks mass limits, paired deck limits, trim, spacing, apron reservation, placement failure, correct stations, and listing-order output. I will implement the documented algorithm directly. Occupied lane span will include prior lengths, hazmat ramp reservations, and inter-plate gaps; a plate's station will exclude its own ramp reservation. Sister trim will be enforced only when both sister lanes were already open before the candidate, matching the explicit exemptions for opening the first and second lanes.
Plan: Rewrite the core data model, strict parser, lane metadata, boarding sort, spacing/mass/trim checks, lane selection, and fold/output logic. Preserve packing by BOARD/name while recording results by original input index. Build and install the binary, then run the sample plus a compact suite covering empty and malformed rolls, height preference, capacities, boarding/station order, rejection, and hazmat spacing.

steps.message:
Analysis: Most behavior is correct, but the hazmat test exposed a subtle double-counting issue. A previous hazmat plate's 100 cm ramp apron already occupies the first required neighbour keep-clear. Therefore incremental spacing for a following plate must subtract that existing apron: hazmat-to-hazmat needs only one additional 100 cm to create the required total 200 cm gap, and hazmat-to-clean needs no additional allocation beyond the existing apron. The current implementation adds the full neighbour gap on top of the apron.
Plan: Correct neighbourGap to return only the additional space not already reserved by the previous plate's ramp apron. Rebuild and verify exact physical gaps from stations, rerun vet and the baseline sample, then finalize.
